comparisons.peer_topic: Data center and cloud computing solutions
comparisons.peer_summary: The company offers a deep portfolio of data center solutions including AI accelerators, CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, SmartNICs, and FPGAs to meet performance requirements for data centers, supercomputers, and cloud environments.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD describe deep portfolio offerings designed to meet the performance requirements of data centers and cloud environments. AVGO provides 'infrastructure software solutions' that offer 'choice and flexibility' for building and managing applications across data center and cloud environments. AMD offers a 'deep portfolio of data center computing solutions' including AI accelerators, CPUs, and GPUs to meet the 'vast computing performance requirements' of data centers and cloud environments. While AVGO focuses on software-defined flexibility and AMD focuses on hardware computing power, both disclosures highlight providing comprehensive solutions to address the complex needs of modern data center infrastructure.

sentences.text: Our infrastructure software solutions offer customers greater choice and flexibility to build, run, manage, connect and protect applications and data at scale across data center and private and hybrid cloud environments.

We offer a deep portfolio of data center computing solutions including AI accelerators, microprocessors (CPUs), graphic processing units (GPUs), data processing units (DPUs), Smart Network Interface Cards (SmartNICs), and field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), to meet the vast computing performance requirements of today's data centers, supercomputers, AI and Machine Learning (ML) data center environments and cloud environments.

comparisons.peer_summary: Beyond CPUs, Intel delivers xPU products including GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs, and accelerators to address diverse workloads and computing needs. The company aims to offer leading products across these different architectural categories.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and Intel describe broad portfolio strategies to address diverse computing needs in data center and cloud environments. AVGO's infrastructure software solutions offer customers flexibility to 'build, run, manage, connect and protect applications and data' across various cloud environments. Similarly, Intel describes an 'xPU approach' delivering a broad portfolio of GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs, and accelerators to meet 'increasingly diverse computing needs' because 'different workloads benefit from different computing architectures.' Both disclosures reflect a strategic focus on providing flexible, diverse options to customers deploying infrastructure.

sentences.text: Our infrastructure software solutions offer customers greater choice and flexibility to build, run, manage, connect and protect applications and data at scale across data center and private and hybrid cloud environments.
Beyond the CPU, we deliver a family of xPU products encompassing client and data center GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs, and other accelerators.
The xPU approach recognizes that different workloads benefit from different computing architectures, and our broad portfolio helps meet our customers' increasingly diverse computing needs.

comparisons.peer_summary: CNBU data center sales were driven by server demand in cloud and enterprise markets, with growth fueled by the shift of infrastructure and workloads to the cloud and the memory-intensive nature of AI data-centric workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and Micron identify the shift of infrastructure and workloads to the cloud as a key driver for their respective data center offerings. AVGO notes its software solutions allow customers to manage data 'at scale across data center and private and hybrid cloud environments,' implying a focus on the architectural benefits of cloud deployment. Micron explicitly states that 'cloud growth continues to be driven by the shift of both infrastructure and workloads from on-premises to the cloud' and that AI workloads are 'memory-centric,' driving demand for its products. Both companies align their data center value propositions with the ongoing migration to cloud architectures.

sentences.text: Our infrastructure software solutions offer customers greater choice and flexibility to build, run, manage, connect and protect applications and data at scale across data center and private and hybrid cloud environments.
Overall cloud growth continues to be driven by the shift of both infrastructure and workloads from on-premises to the cloud.

Cloud-native workloads are drivers of growth through use-cases like intelligent edge devices capable of AI and augmented reality that store and access data in the cloud or rely on the cloud for compute capability.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA's data-center-scale offerings comprise compute and networking solutions that can scale to tens of thousands of GPU-accelerated servers functioning as a single giant computer, an architecture necessary for modern AI application development and deployment.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and NVIDIA describe comprehensive infrastructure solutions designed for data center and cloud environments, emphasizing scale and flexibility. AVGO focuses on software solutions that provide 'choice and flexibility to build, run, manage, connect and protect applications and data' across hybrid clouds, while NVIDIA describes 'compute and networking solutions' that scale to 'tens of thousands of GPU-accelerated servers' to function as a 'single giant computer' for AI applications. Both highlight the capability to handle large-scale workloads, though AVGO emphasizes software-defined flexibility and NVIDIA emphasizes hardware-scale aggregation.

sentences.text: Our infrastructure software solutions offer customers greater choice and flexibility to build, run, manage, connect and protect applications and data at scale across data center and private and hybrid cloud environments.

Our data-center-scale offerings are comprised of compute and networking solutions that can scale to tens of thousands of GPU-accelerated servers interconnected to function as a single giant computer; this type of data center architecture and scale is needed for the development and deployment of modern AI applications.

comparisons.peer_topic: AI research focus and on-device capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: The company conducts broad research and development across AI, including generative AI, with the goal of advancing core capabilities to run on-device and scaling them across industries, leveraging over a decade of investments focused on power efficiency and personalization.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and Qualcomm discuss the advancement of AI capabilities across different infrastructure layers. AVGO highlights its infrastructure software solutions that allow customers to 'protect applications and data at scale' in cloud environments, which includes supporting AI workloads. Qualcomm discusses its R&D focus on advancing AI 'core capabilities to run on-device' and scaling them across industries. While AVGO's disclosure focuses on the software infrastructure layer for data centers and cloud, and Qualcomm focuses on on-device AI execution, both are part of the broader ecosystem of AI infrastructure development and deployment strategies.
